```{r}
overlapSums <- function(x, y, z, na.rm=FALSE) {
  stopifnot(class(x)=="GRanges")
  stopifnot(class(y)=="GRanges")
  stopifnot(class(z)=="numeric" | class(z)=="integer")
  stopifnot(length(x)==length(z))
  ov <- as.matrix(findOverlaps(y, x))
  ovSums <- rep(as.numeric(NA), length(y))
  ovSums[unique(ov[,1])] <- viewSums(Views(z[ov[,2]], ranges(Rle(ov[,1]))), na.rm=na.rm)
  ovSums
}


overlapRatios <- function(x, y, C, cov, minCov, na.rm=FALSE) {
  C.sum <- overlapSums(x, y, values(x)[[C]], na.rm=na.rm)
  cov.sum <- overlapSums(x, y, values(x)[[cov]], na.rm=na.rm)
  ov_all <- as.data.frame(findOverlaps(y, x)) 
  number_of_CpGs <- rle(ov_all[,1])$lengths #--- total number of CpGs per region
  CpG_ov_regions <- x[ov_all$subjectHits] #--- coverage of CpGs overlapping regions
  ov_all$cov <- as.numeric(values(CpG_ov_regions)[[cov]])
  ov_all$cov_binary<-as.numeric(ifelse(ov_all$cov>=minCov, 1, 0))
  number_of_CpGs_minCov <- as.numeric(tapply(ov_all$cov_binary, ov_all$queryHits, FUN=sum))
  CpGs_covered <- as.numeric(number_of_CpGs_minCov) / as.numeric(number_of_CpGs)
  rat <- as.data.frame(C.sum/cov.sum)
  rat_cov<-cbind(rat, CpGs_covered)
  colnames(rat_cov) <- c("rat", "CpGs_covered")
  rat_cov$rat[rat_cov$CpGs_covered < 0.5] <- NA
  rat_cov[,1]
}
```

## Non-conversion rate
#---Lambda DNA
```{r}
lambda <- bt[grep("chrLambda", seqnames(bt)),] # replace with the actual lambda name in your genome
puc19 <- bt[grep("pUC19", seqnames(bt)),] # replace with the actual pUC19 name in your genome

lambda <- as.data.frame(lambda)
lambda$start <- as.numeric(lambda$start)
lambda_CpGs <- GRanges(lambda$seqnames, IRanges(lambda$start, width=2), strand="*")
values(lambda_CpGs) <- as.data.frame(lambda)[,-c(1:5)]

col<-seq(1, ncol(mcols(lambda_CpGs)), by=2)
names <- sub('\\..*', '', colnames(mcols(lambda_CpGs))[col])
col <- setNames(col, names)

mc_score <- mapply(function(a, b){as.numeric(mcols(lambda_CpGs)[, a]) / as.numeric(mcols(lambda_CpGs)[, b])}, a = col, b = col+1) # calculates methylation ratio using .C and .cov of adjacent columns 
mc_score<-as.data.frame(mc_score)

lambda_m <- melt(mc_score, measure.vars = colnames(mc_score))
mean <- ddply(lambda_m, "variable", summarise, rating.mean=mean(value))
mean$rating.mean <- mean$rating.mean*100
colnames(mean) <- c("sample", "non-conversion_rate")
mean
```

###---Average mC lineplot
```{r}

# Reshape and calculate means/sem
mc_plot <- mc_score %>%
 as.data.frame() %>%
 mutate(site = row_number()) %>%
 pivot_longer(-site, names_to = "sample_rep", values_to = "mC") %>%
 mutate(sample = gsub("_r[12]$", "", sample_rep)) %>%
 group_by(sample) %>%
 summarise(mean_mC = mean(mC, na.rm = TRUE), 
           sem_mC = sd(mC, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()), .groups = 'drop') %>%
 mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = c("dunnart_sperm", "dunnart_d9", "dunnart_d10", 
                                          "dunnart_d12", "dunnart_d13", "dunnart_liver")))


setwd("/Users/ksenia/Documents/Lab_Garvan/projects/marsupials/EMseq_final_genome/mC/figures/")

print(ggplot(mc_plot, aes(x = sample, y = mean_mC)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_mC - sem_mC, ymax = mean_mC + sem_mC, group = 1), 
              alpha = 0.4, fill = "#3498db") +
```

# Performing PCA analysis
```{r}
#https://blog.bioturing.com/2018/06/18/how-to-read-pca-biplots-and-scree-plots/
  
# You should scale data whenever your variables differ 
# by orders of magnitude, as they do here.
# Transcription data usually varies over orders of 
# magnitude, so scaling is appropriate.
# We'll run PCA with prcomp (SVD-based), with and without 
# scaling to unit variance
#unscaled = prcomp(USArrests)
#scaled = prcomp(USArrests, scale = TRUE)

#perform PCA calculation
pca <- prcomp(t) #scale = TRUE


# If you look at your prcomp output, you'll see it reports
# Standard deviations and Rotation. The screeplot plots variances (eigenvalues),
# but remember that sqrt(Variance) = StDev. So, recovering the
# variances in the screeplot is easy:
stats <- pca 
summary(stats)
stats$var = stats$sdev * stats$sdev


# It's similarly easy to get the proportion of variance reported
# in the summary
prop <- stats$var/sum(stats$var)
PC <- c(1:length(prop))
df <- cbind(PC, prop)
df <- as.data.frame(df)
df$PC <- paste0("PC", df$PC)
colnames(df) <- c("PC","Proportion_of_variance")

df$Proportion_of_variance <- as.numeric(df$Proportion_of_variance * 100)
df$Proportion_of_variance <- as.numeric(format(df$Proportion_of_variance, scientific=FALSE))
df$Proportion_of_variance <- round(df$Proportion_of_variance, digits = 2)

df$PC <- factor(df$PC, levels = unique(df$PC))

setwd("/Users/ksenia/Documents/Lab_Garvan/projects/marsupials/EMseq_final_genome/mC/bins1kb/figures/")
pdf("PCA_all_5mC_bins1kb_scree_plot_prop_of_variance.pdf", useDingbats=FALSE, width=12, height=8)
print(ggplot(data = df, aes(x = PC, y = Proportion_of_variance)) +
        geom_point(size = 6) +
        #geom_label(aes(label = Proportion_of_variance), position = "identity") +
        geom_line())
dev.off()


# Looking at the biplots is also informative
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
biplot(pca)

#visualize data using two principal components
#biplot(pca,var.axes=FALSE,ylabs=NULL)
#biplot(pca, scale = TRUE)


#scree plot
#A scree plot displays how much variation each principal component captures from the data
#To deal with a not-so-ideal scree plot curve, there are a couple ways:

#Kaiser rule: pick PCs with eigenvalues of at least 1.
#Proportion of variance plot: the selected PCs should be able to describe at least 80% of the variance.

#If you end up with too many principal components (more than 3), PCA might not be the best way to visualize your data. Instead, consider other dimension reduction techniques, such as t-SNE and MDS.


setwd("/Users/ksenia/Documents/Lab_Garvan/projects/marsupials/EMseq_final_genome/mC/bins1kb/figures/")
pdf("PCA_all_5mC_bins1kb_scree_plot.pdf", useDingbats=FALSE, width=12, height=8)
print(screeplot(pca,type="lines"))
dev.off()

# create data frame with scores
scores = as.data.frame(pca$x)
rownames(scores) <- as.factor(rownames(scores))
scores$sample <- row.names(scores)

scores$sample <- ifelse(grepl("NB", scores$sample, ignore.case = TRUE), "African", "European")
```
